questions.summary: Accept or reject five statements with a short motivation: (a) significant test result so invest in costly process change; (b) 95% CI for % defectives [1.4%, 2.2%] so the process cannot deliver < 1%; (c) a population mean can in theory be estimated to any chosen precision; (d) cluster sampling never shows non-response bias; (e) testing at 1% significance requires a 99% CI.
topics: interpretation of a confidence interval for a proportion
duality of tests and confidence intervals (one- vs two-sided)

course_pages.why: pitfalls of statistical testing, incl. significance vs relevance (a)
a result must also have practical meaning (a)
definition/interpretation of a CI; CI for a proportion (b)
confidence vs accuracy for a given sample size (c)
cluster sampling; non-response bias and representativity (d)
CI as a test; significance of a one-sided CI-based test (e)
one- vs two-sided tests; link between tests and CIs (e)

questions.calculator_note: Conceptual. A CI-for-proportion calculator could illustrate (b) but is not needed to answer.

topics: confidence interval for a ratio of variances

sheet 'F' (F density illustration)
Excel statistical functions (F.INVERSE / F.VERDELING)

questions.summary: Electrolytic capacitors (nominal 800 uF; non-conforming if < 720 uF; lots of 100; on average 2 in 40 non-conforming; mean capacity 820 uF; 175,3 orders/week of 3,6 lots). Random variables B (orders/week), T (time between orders), C (capacity), X (conformity), D (non-conforming per lot): (a) place each variable's expected value under its distribution family (normal, Bernoulli, exponential, uniform, Poisson, binomial); (b) for which variables is the i.i.d. idea unrealistic, and why; (c) compute Var[C].
topics: distribution families (Poisson, exponential, normal, Bernoulli, binomial)
normal quantile: sigma from a tail probability

independence (b)
random variables, distributions, probabilistic model (a)
